composition_notes: Keep all five participants viable until the formal evidence rules are applied. The narrative supplies no checksum values, privileged role labels, or answer cues; the formalizer and deterministic code must derive the result. Avoid treating room order, name, seniority, or any single record as a shortcut.
intended_answer: Return the participant selected by the deterministic comparison of each participant’s relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses with the accepted iterated modular checksum; no external role designation is required.
premise: At the North Annex conservation workshop, a water-damaged astronomical astrolabe is being traced from the intake bay through the imaging room, solvent bench, drying vault, and documentation office. Five workshop participants—Mara, Ivo, Selene, Tomas, and Priya—left overlapping records: handoff notes, badge times, tool-use logs, condition observations, tray positions, and sign-off entries. The records contain agreements and contradictions about who handled which fragment, when each transfer occurred, what caused the damage to spread, where the artifact rested, the order of treatment steps, and whether each action followed the workshop protocol. The incident ledger has an accepted iterated modular checksum, calculated under the benchmark’s local deterministic rules from six evidence statuses for each participant: relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol. The locally defined concept certified restoration lead means exactly the one participant whose six evidence statuses produce that accepted checksum.
setting_summary: A conservation workshop traces a damaged artifact through several rooms using intertwined physical records and procedural logs, rather than investigating a crime.
target_question: Which participant’s six-stream iterated modular checksum matches the incident’s accepted checksum under the local rules?
